<reflection>
After two experiments, the cumulative negative log-likelihood values show that M7 fits best, followed by M17 and M16. However, many mechanisms remain within a narrow range (differences of a few units), indicating that discrimination is still limited. The second experiment (higher catalyst) helped separate some mechanisms but not decisively. The aim for this turn is to design an experiment that further discriminates among the plausible mechanisms, particularly by probing the effect of product, which is present in several mechanisms as a reactant in reverse, inhibition, or deactivation steps.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Introducing initial product will test for reversibility, product inhibition, and product-induced deactivation. By comparing kinetics with and without initial product under otherwise identical conditions (substrate=1.0 M, catalyst=0.01 M), we can isolate product effects. Mechanisms with reversible catalytic steps (e.g., M1, M2, etc.) will show reduced net forward rate. Mechanisms with product inhibition (e.g., M12, M17) may exhibit slower rates or altered time profiles. Mechanisms with product-dependent deactivation (e.g., M12, M17) could show faster catalyst decay. This experiment avoids extreme conditions (product concentration is moderate at 0.2 M) and targets a different aspect of the kinetics, providing orthogonal information to the previous catalyst variation.
</hypothesis>
